study_identification_part.si_4_title: Age-atypical brain functional networks in autism spectrum disorder: a normative modeling approach

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used the ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange) dataset, which is a large-scale open-access neuroimaging dataset for ASD containing resting-state fMRI data from 1495 individuals collected at 17 data acquisition centers. The specific version (ABIDE-I or ABIDE-II) is not explicitly stated, but based on context (reference to Di Martino et al., 2014 and dataset size), this appears to be ABIDE-I.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The ABIDE dataset is a large-scale open-access neuroimaging dataset for ASD, which currently includes resting-state fMRI data from 1495 individuals collected at 17 data acquisition centers." ... "All the data analyzed in this study were sourced from the ABIDE dataset."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Jiang2024.pdf.md: Methods and materials / Participants, L92; S0033291724000138sup001.docx.md: L1-3

answer.ABIDE: normative model training/testing (TD group) and clinical research application (ASD group)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The TD (typically developed) group from ABIDE (N=642) was used to construct the normative model of age-related functional connectivity development using LOESS regression. The ASD group from ABIDE (N=576) was used as the clinical application cohort to assess individual-level deviations from the normative model and correlations with behavioral symptoms (SRS scores). No separate train/validation/test split was explicitly described for the normative model; the entire TD cohort appears to have been used for model construction.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Using a world-wide multi-site database known as Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange, we analyzed individuals with ASD and typically developed (TD) controls (total n = 1218) aged 5-40 years, generating individualized whole-brain network functional connectivity (FC) maps of age-related atypicality in ASD. We then used local polynomial regression to estimate a networkwise normative model of development..."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Jiang2024.pdf.md: Abstract, L45-48; Methods and materials / Constructing age-related normative models, L94-100

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was constructed using the TD (typically developed) group. The total TD sample size was 642 after exclusion of left-handed participants and those with poor scan quality. The original ABIDE dataset included 836 TD individuals before exclusion. No explicit train/validation/test split was reported; the entire TD cohort appears to have been used for normative model estimation using LOESS regression with bootstrapping for reliability assessment.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "After exclusion, the sample size was 642 for the TD group and 576 for the ASD group." ... "The dataset includes 659 datasets from patients with ASD and 836 datasets from TD individuals."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Jiang2024.pdf.md: Table 1, L76-85; Methods and materials / Participants, L92; S0033291724000138sup001.docx.md: L3

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics for the TD group used in normative model construction are directly reported in Table 1. Mean age was 15.34 years (SD = 8.033), with a range of 5-40 years and median of 13 years. IQR values were not reported. No separate train-phase statistics were provided as no train/test split was explicitly described.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex distribution for the TD group specifically was not reported. The study mentions in the Limitations section that the overall sample has few female participants with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 5:1, but this appears to refer to the combined ASD+TD sample or possibly the ASD sample specifically. No breakdown by group (TD vs ASD) for sex is provided in Table 1 or elsewhere in the paper.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Fourth, although this study has a large sample size, it does not encompass the very early developmental period or the very late adulthood period; it also has few female participants, with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 5:1."
